tagline: A reclaimed lake became a refuge; bridges replaced a sound ferry
intro: The Alligator River Route appears in North Carolina’s scenic-byway guide, whose program highlights the state’s history, geography and culture. Lake Mattamuskeet is a shallow coastal lake on the Albemarle-Pamlico Peninsula, averaging two to three feet deep. At Manns Harbor, two bridges cross Croatan Sound to Roanoke Island.

A ferry carried traffic across the sound before the William B. Umstead Bridge connection of 1957. By 1996, two hurricane evacuations had exposed the limits of the two-lane crossing. Planning for another bridge followed, to ease congestion and provide an additional evacuation route. The four-lane Virginia Dare Memorial Bridge opened on August 16, 2002.

New Holland lies on Lake Mattamuskeet’s southern shore. Columbia stands on the Scuppernong River, while Manns Harbor occupies the western bank of Croatan Sound. At the sound, the William B. Umstead Bridge leads toward Manteo; the Virginia Dare Memorial Bridge offers the crossing farther south.

moments.title: Lake Mattamuskeet
moments.text: New Holland’s name came from an attempt to turn the lakebed into land. Between 1911 and 1934, three private investment companies worked with the Mattamuskeet Drainage District to drain the 50,000-acre lake for farms, homes and commerce. They built a pumping plant and dredged 130 miles of navigable canals. The third private owner sold the lake property to the federal government in 1934 for a migratory bird refuge. The lake and old town site are now within Mattamuskeet National Wildlife Refuge, a wintering area for waterfowl. The surviving brick pump station was remodeled in 1934 as headquarters and hotel accommodation after the federal acquisition; its new use followed the end of drainage.

moments.title: Columbia
moments.text: Columbia began as Elizabethtown on the Scuppernong River in 1793 and became the Tyrrell County seat in 1799. Its historic district includes the 1903 brick courthouse, built with arched windows and a hipped roof. Somerset Place, a separate historic site near Columbia, dates from 1785. More than 300 enslaved men, women and children of African descent lived there; the site interprets their lives and work alongside the plantation’s Collins family history. The courthouse porch is a later addition, dating to the 1970s, with paired columns supporting its flat roof. The older building’s windows have both round and segmental arches.

moments.title: Manns Harbor
moments.text: Two bridges now make the crossing once served by a ferry at Manns Harbor. The William B. Umstead Bridge is the two-lane crossing; the Virginia Dare Memorial Bridge provides four lanes farther south. The older bridge also serves migrating purple martins, which roost on beams beneath it in July and August. In 2007, the Coastal Carolina Purple Martin Society asked for a lower speed limit at dawn and dusk, when birds swarm. The change reduced bird deaths. The newer bridge gives traffic a route onward to Bodie Island without going through Manteo, changing the approach to the Outer Banks once again.
